evidence.claim: Putin framed the February 24 invasion as a necessary security move, warned that a direct attack on Russia would bring catastrophic consequences, and said Ukraine should not be allowed to acquire nuclear weapons.
evidence.title: 'No other option': Excerpts of Putin's speech declaring war
evidence.excerpt: Putin framed the February 24 invasion as a necessary security move, warned that a direct attack on Russia would bring catastrophic consequences, and said Ukraine should not be allowed to acquire nuclear weapons.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct transcript excerpt published the day of the invasion, translated from the Kremlin recording.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributed to Putin as the speaking president.
contrary_evidence: The speech is self-justifying propaganda, not an independent account of the war's causes.

evidence.claim: Putin's recognition decrees for the self-proclaimed DPR and LPR said Ukraine had refused peaceful settlement under the Minsk agreements and ordered the Russian military to perform peacekeeping functions there.
evidence.title: Путин поручил Минобороны РФ обеспечить поддержание мира в ДНР и ЛНР
evidence.excerpt: Putin's recognition decrees for the self-proclaimed DPR and LPR said Ukraine had refused peaceful settlement under the Minsk agreements and ordered the Russian military to perform peacekeeping functions there.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Russian-language publication of the decree text on the day it was signed.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential decree attributable to Putin.
contrary_evidence: The decrees were widely treated internationally as a prelude to aggression rather than peacekeeping.

evidence.claim: Kommersant reported that Russia said it would reduce military activity on the Kyiv and Chernihiv fronts after the Istanbul talks and had received Ukrainian written proposals on neutrality and security guarantees.
evidence.title: Итоги российско-украинских переговоров в Стамбуле. Главное
evidence.excerpt: Kommersant reported that Russia said it would reduce military activity on the Kyiv and Chernihiv fronts after the Istanbul talks and had received Ukrainian written proposals on neutrality and security guarantees.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Russian-language contemporaneous summary of the talks and Russian claims about de-escalation.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in the March 2022 negotiation window.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Russian negotiating position under Putin.
contrary_evidence: The reduction was framed as conditional and reversible, not a durable ceasefire.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said the Russian invasion was marked by indiscriminate attacks on civilian areas and protected objects such as hospitals, and that the Russian government should take responsibility.
evidence.title: Russia commits indiscriminate attacks during the invasion of Ukraine
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said the Russian invasion was marked by indiscriminate attacks on civilian areas and protected objects such as hospitals, and that the Russian government should take responsibility.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Immediate independent field research published two days after the invasion.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The attacks were carried out by Russian forces in Putin's invasion.
contrary_evidence: Amnesty's conclusion is rights-based and does not itself determine criminal liability.

evidence.claim: Amnesty found that Russian and Russian-controlled forces unlawfully transferred or deported civilians from occupied parts of Ukraine and subjected them to abusive filtration procedures.
evidence.title: Ukraine: “Like A Prison Convoy”: Russia’s Unlawful Transfer And Abuse of Civilians In Ukraine During ‘Filtration’
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty found that Russian and Russian-controlled forces unlawfully transferred or deported civilians from occupied parts of Ukraine and subjected them to abusive filtration procedures.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed 2022 investigative report with a direct summary finding.
evidence.period_fit: Late-2022 occupation governance and civilian transfer practices.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Applies to Russian-controlled structures operating under Putin's occupation policy.
contrary_evidence: The report includes Russian-controlled forces, not only Moscow-commanded regular troops.

evidence.claim: The ICC opened an investigation into the situation in Ukraine on 2 March 2022, and the page later states there are reasonable grounds to believe Putin bears responsibility for unlawful deportation and transfer of children from occupied areas of Ukraine.
evidence.title: Ukraine | International Criminal Court
evidence.excerpt: The ICC opened an investigation into the situation in Ukraine on 2 March 2022, and the page later states there are reasonable grounds to believe Putin bears responsibility for unlawful deportation and transfer of children from occupied areas of Ukraine.
evidence.source_locator: situation overview and Putin suspect section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official court page summarizing the investigation and suspect determinations.
evidence.period_fit: The investigation began in 2022 and concerns conduct from 24 February 2022 onward.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly names Putin in the suspect section.
contrary_evidence: The arrest-warrant findings were issued later, in 2023, even though they concern 2022 conduct.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Putin's chief envoy on Ukraine told him a provisional deal with Kyiv would satisfy Russia's demand that Ukraine stay out of NATO, but Putin rejected it, expanded objectives toward annexing Ukrainian territory, and pressed ahead with the military campaign.
evidence.title: Exclusive-As war began, Putin rejected a Ukraine peace deal recommended by his aide: sources
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Putin's chief envoy on Ukraine told him a provisional deal with Kyiv would satisfy Russia's demand that Ukraine stay out of NATO, but Putin rejected it, expanded objectives toward annexing Ukrainian territory, and pressed ahead with the military campaign.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting based on sources close to the Russian leadership; the Kremlin denied it, so attribution is strong but not independently documented.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: the decision is explicitly attributed to Putin by sources close to his leadership and concerns his choice over available peace terms.
contrary_evidence: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the report had no relation to reality
A Ukrainian adviser said Russia was never interested in a peaceful settlement

evidence.claim: Amnesty said Russian soldiers subjected Ukrainian civilians to abusive filtration, many displaced people reached Russia or Russian-occupied territory involuntarily, and vulnerable groups including children, older people, and people with disabilities were blocked or constrained from fleeing.
evidence.title: Russia: 'Filtration' of Ukrainian civilians a 'shocking violation' of people forced to flee war
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said Russian soldiers subjected Ukrainian civilians to abusive filtration, many displaced people reached Russia or Russian-occupied territory involuntarily, and vulnerable groups including children, older people, and people with disabilities were blocked or constrained from fleeing.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct Amnesty field reporting contemporaneous with the occupation; strong on the mechanism and victim groups, though based on interviews and UN verification rather than Russian admission.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: the abusive screening and transfer regime operated in Russian-occupied territory under Russian military control.
contrary_evidence: Russia portrayed movements as evacuations or temporary placement rather than forced transfer

evidence.claim: The UN human-rights mission said Russian armed forces arbitrarily executed or attacked civilians in the early weeks of the invasion, causing hundreds of civilian deaths in Kyiv, Chernihiv, and Sumy oblasts between 24 February and 6 April 2022.
evidence.title: Доповідь ООН описує свавільні страти та напади на окремих цивільних осіб із боку російських військ на півночі України з лютого до квітня
evidence.publisher: Моніторингова місія ООН з прав людини в Україні
evidence.excerpt: The UN human-rights mission said Russian armed forces arbitrarily executed or attacked civilians in the early weeks of the invasion, causing hundreds of civilian deaths in Kyiv, Chernihiv, and Sumy oblasts between 24 February and 6 April 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official UN monitoring report with concrete casualty totals and time/place bounds; strong independent corroboration of unlawful conduct.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in-period, February-April 2022, reported in December 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: the conduct is attributed to Russian troops acting under Putin's wartime command authority.
contrary_evidence: Russia disputed blame for civilian deaths and denied unlawful targeting

evidence.claim: The Council of Europe suspended the Russian Federation from its rights of representation because of its armed attack on Ukraine.
evidence.title: Council of Europe suspends Russia's rights of representation
evidence.excerpt: The Council of Europe suspended the Russian Federation from its rights of representation because of its armed attack on Ukraine.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official institutional action taken immediately after the invasion; strong for the international reaction to Russia's conduct.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: this is an institutional sanction in response to Putin's attack, not a first-hand record of a secret decision.
contrary_evidence: Russia maintained that its military action was legitimate self-defense

evidence.claim: Putin said Russia was open to negotiations over the war in Ukraine, but the report noted he blamed Kyiv and Western backers for the lack of talks, demanded terms that would require Ukraine to accept Russia's annexation claims, and cited Washington's view that this was posturing amid persistent Russian attacks.
evidence.title: Putin says Russia ready to negotiate over Ukraine, Kyiv voices doubts
evidence.excerpt: Putin said Russia was open to negotiations over the war in Ukraine, but the report noted he blamed Kyiv and Western backers for the lack of talks, demanded terms that would require Ukraine to accept Russia's annexation claims, and cited Washington's view that this was posturing amid persistent Russian attacks.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting on a direct Putin statement, with immediate U.S. and Ukrainian pushback; strong for the claim and its contested credibility.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: the quote is directly Putin's, but it is a conditional negotiation stance on terms he controlled.
contrary_evidence: U.S. State Department called it posturing
Ukraine said Russia did not want talks

evidence.claim: The ICJ found Ukraine had a plausible right not to be subjected to Russian military operations under the claimed genocide-prevention rationale and ordered Russia to immediately suspend the military operations it commenced on 24 February 2022.
evidence.title: Allegations of Genocide under the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide (Ukraine v. Russian Federation), Order of 16 March 2022
evidence.excerpt: The ICJ found Ukraine had a plausible right not to be subjected to Russian military operations under the claimed genocide-prevention rationale and ordered Russia to immediately suspend the military operations it commenced on 24 February 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary international court order with direct legal findings and binding provisional measures.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Putin's launched invasion and Russia's wartime justification for it.
contrary_evidence: Russia disputed the court's framing and the order did not reach the merits of the case.

evidence.claim: The General Assembly demanded that Russia immediately end its invasion of Ukraine, unconditionally withdraw all forces, reverse its February 21 decision on the Donetsk and Luhansk regions, and allow humanitarian access and civilian protection.
evidence.title: General Assembly Overwhelmingly Adopts Resolution Demanding Russian Federation Immediately End Illegal Use of Force in Ukraine, Withdraw All Troops
evidence.excerpt: The General Assembly demanded that Russia immediately end its invasion of Ukraine, unconditionally withdraw all forces, reverse its February 21 decision on the Donetsk and Luhansk regions, and allow humanitarian access and civilian protection.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official UN General Assembly press release summarizing the adopted resolution and vote.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Putin's invasion and subsequent escalation posture.
contrary_evidence: The resolution was nonbinding, so it is evidence of international rejection rather than enforced compliance.

evidence.claim: The General Assembly condemned Russia's attempted annexation of Donetsk, Kherson, Luhansk, and Zaporizhzhia and demanded that Russia immediately withdraw and reverse those decisions.
evidence.title: With 143 Votes in Favour, 5 Against, General Assembly Adopts Resolution Condemning Russian Federation’s Annexation of Four Eastern Ukraine Regions
evidence.excerpt: The General Assembly condemned Russia's attempted annexation of Donetsk, Kherson, Luhansk, and Zaporizhzhia and demanded that Russia immediately withdraw and reverse those decisions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official UN General Assembly press release on a recorded vote and resolution text.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Putin's annexation decisions.
contrary_evidence: The resolution is nonbinding, but it remains strong evidence of international legal and political repudiation.

evidence.claim: Russia, Ukraine, Türkiye, and the UN inaugurated a Joint Coordination Centre in Istanbul to operationalize the Black Sea Grain Initiative and establish a humanitarian maritime corridor for safe exports of grain, foodstuffs, and fertilizers.
evidence.title: Joint Coordination Centre opens in Istanbul to facilitate safe export of commercial foodstuffs and fertilizers from Ukrainian ports
evidence.excerpt: Russia, Ukraine, Türkiye, and the UN inaugurated a Joint Coordination Centre in Istanbul to operationalize the Black Sea Grain Initiative and establish a humanitarian maritime corridor for safe exports of grain, foodstuffs, and fertilizers.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UN press release with concrete implementation details, named participants, and a clear humanitarian purpose.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Putin's government through Russia's direct participation in the agreement and JCC implementation.
contrary_evidence: The initiative was a limited humanitarian corridor, not a general shift away from the broader war.
